name: Cyprus
summary: EU citizens only register. Non-EU citizens (US and others) can get permanent residence by investing EUR 300,000 and showing EUR 50,000 of income, or through the no-investment Category F with EUR 9,568 of foreign income (but a multi-year queue), or a digital nomad visa at EUR 42,000 a year. Citizenship by investment ended in 2020.
naturalisation: Under Law 149(I)/2023 (from 19 December 2023): 12 months of lawful residence immediately before applying plus 7 years of lawful residence in the preceding 10, so about 8 years; Greek B1 and a civics test (60%). A faster 4 to 5 year path exists for highly skilled workers who pass Greek and civics exams.
dual_citizenship_note: One source says Cyprus allows dual citizenship without restriction; not confirmed from an official text.

routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 183-day rule or the 60-day rule, separate from immigration status.
routes.name: EU free movement (MEU1 registration)
routes.summary: EU citizens register with the Migration Department after 3 months and get permanent residence after 5 years.
routes.requirements: Valid ID or passport; workers, self-employed or economically inactive with resources and health cover. Registration certificate MEU1; permanent residence on form MEU3 after 5 years of continuous legal residence.

sources.title: Your Europe: Residence rights in another EU country

routes.fees_note: EUR 500 for the main application covering spouse and minor children, plus EUR 70 per person for the Aliens Registration Certificate; adult children EUR 500 each.
routes.processing_time: About 2 months officially, about 6 months in practice
routes.family: Spouse and minor children included; adult children apply separately.
routes.tax_note: A permit does not make you tax resident; Cyprus non-dom rules apply once you are resident.
routes.name: Fast-track permanent residence by investment (Regulation 6(2))
routes.summary: Permanent residence for a EUR 300,000 property or business investment plus EUR 50,000 a year of income from abroad.
routes.requirements: Investment of at least EUR 300,000 plus VAT in new property, Cyprus company share capital or a CySEC-supervised fund; secured annual income from abroad of at least EUR 50,000, plus EUR 15,000 for a spouse and EUR 10,000 per child under 18. Investor and spouse cannot work in Cyprus except as directors of the invested company. Annual proof of investment and health insurance; criminal record every 3 years. Permit ends after 2 years of absence. Tighter rules were signalled but not published (per GK Law, 13 October 2026).
routes.physical_presence: Visit at least once every 2 years (permit ends after 2 years' absence)

routes.fees_note: Not sourced for Category F separately.
routes.processing_time: Several years in 2026; the Department is still examining applications filed years earlier
routes.family: Dependants add EUR 4,613 a year each to the income test.
routes.name: Category F permanent residence (secured foreign income)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for people with secured income from abroad of at least EUR 9,568 a year; no investment, but decisions take years.
routes.requirements: Secured income from abroad of at least EUR 9,568 a year plus EUR 4,613 per dependant; Cyprus bank account; owned or rented accommodation; from 1 September 2026 listed medical test results. No work in Cyprus. Regulation 5(f).
routes.physical_presence: Visit at least once every 2 years

sources.title: Amendments to the Cyprus permanent residence programme (Category F)

routes.family: Spouse and children via the income uplift.
routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 183-day or 60-day rule. The non-dom regime can exempt dividends and some interest for up to 17 years.
routes.name: Digital nomad visa
routes.summary: For remote workers earning at least EUR 3,500 net a month from employers or clients outside Cyprus; capped at 500 permits.
routes.requirements: Stable net income of at least EUR 3,500 a month (EUR 42,000 a year), +20% for a spouse and +15% per child (per one guide). Work only for non-Cypriot employers or clients. Scheme capped at 500 permits (another source says 1,000). First permit 1 year, renewable up to 2 more years.

routes.status_note: Abolished effective 1 November 2020; no replacement investor-citizenship scheme exists. Investors now take residence then naturalise.
routes.name: Citizenship by investment (Cyprus Investment Programme)
routes.summary: The programme that gave a passport for a EUR 2 million investment no longer exists.
routes.requirements: Closed. Sources agree it ended on 1 November 2020; the former EUR 2 million figure is from general knowledge, not the sources cited.

routes.name: Work permits (employment)
routes.summary: Non-EU workers need an employer to apply for an employment permit for a specific job; quotas and sector rules apply.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Cyprus; no fixed day count sourced
